x: Mike Stearman was present to defend his 880 yards Junior title, but he was beaten by a newcomer to our ranks in Gerry Trower, with Bob Wolton third.

Geoff Goode and Brian Trower were first two home in the mile and Trower also won the Javelin event, much to his surprise ! Jim Purdy won the High Jump and also gained third place in the Javelin, while Frank Kemp won the Shott Putt and it was a case of everyone having a go at everything !
One of our juniors, Brian Trower, had hung on to the back of the bunch and ran well on the way back to finish 8th. Herbert was the winner in 23.56, with Smart 24.5 and Short 24.17.
The lead changed several times first Trower, then Masters. Short took over at 3 miles and then Maynard came through at about 4 miles and strolled home untroubled.
John Burr 5th, gave us a good start. 6th was Johnny Butley, first man home for Surrey A.C. and then four more Bels., Masters, Tooby Trower and Bagnall.

After the first half mile we had Masters, Walker and Bagnall in the first 20, with Patterson Baulch, Short, Trower and Bedford in the twenties, and although positions changed a bit, our scoring six were always placed well in the first thirty.
Masters then pulled the "A" Team up to 4th place but Brian Trower showed his lack of recent racing with a rather slow time which contributed greatly to our subsequent defeat.
Half way round the first lap, Bagnall, Paterson, Short, Masters and Baulch were all between 20th and 30th in that order and Gebbett and Trower were in the next dozen.
